## Tours with an evening samba and capoeira show in Rio de Janeiro

The [evening samba and capoeira show](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-samba-capoeira-night-show/) gives you a night of Brazilian music and staged dance traditions. The standalone excursion features live instruments and drums, dancers in colorful costumes, acrobatic capoeira elements and a transfer back to the hotel after the performance. **Dinner is available as an extra**, so it cannot be treated as included in every version.

Our selection features {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} directly linked to this particular excursion. Such modules may be optional: seeing the show's name on a tour does not guarantee admission is covered by the base price. Check the inclusions of each multi-day itinerary before choosing.

## What audiences will see at the evening performance

Samba is part of Brazil's musical culture, while capoeira combines movements, kicks, evasions and acrobatics with rhythm and music. Capoeira originated as an Afro-Brazilian practice and extends beyond performance art: the traditional capoeira circle, *roda de capoeira*, was inscribed on UNESCO's list of Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2014.

The evening excursion presents these elements on stage. Attending the show **is not a capoeira lesson** and does not itself involve visitors taking part in a traditional roda. The exact artists, venue and performance duration depend on the selected location; they are not fixed terms in Ada Tours' source description.

## Itineraries offering the evening show

### “Luxury Brazil”: a free day in Rio

[“Luxury Brazil”](/multi-country/tour/luxury-brazil/) is an 11-day program. It includes a free day in Rio, after which a range of optional excursions is listed, including the evening show. Other city activities are offered alongside it. It is best seen as one way to spend a free evening, with admission and payment agreed separately.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_luxury_brazil_11d}}

### Brazil, Iguazu and Pantanal: an evening before a wider journey

The [12-day tour through Rio, Iguazu, Pantanal and Búzios](/brazil/tour/brazil-rio-foz-do-iguacu-pantanal-buzios-12-days/) also lists the evening show among linked excursion modules. The trip reaches far beyond Rio, with dedicated days for nature areas and beaches. Compare the timing of the performance with later flights and road transfers so you have enough energy for the main itinerary.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_rio_de_janeiro_foz_do_iguacu_pantanal_buzios}}

### A coffee-themed journey through Brazil

The [private Brazil coffee tour](/brazil/tour/brazil-private-coffee-tour/) also lists the evening show as a linked excursion. Coffee is the focus of that trip, while an evening performance adds a cultural experience in Rio. It illustrates the difference between the reason for choosing the tour and an optional evening activity: coffee shapes the journey, while samba and capoeira are an additional experience.

{{catalog.tourTable:tour_source_kofe_tur_v_brazilii}}

Other linked options include tours with [beach time in Búzios](/brazil/tour/tropical-brazil-rio-buzios/) and journeys through several countries. See [all Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) for a wider comparison; this page specifically selects tours with a registered link to this evening show.

## Show with dinner or without: what to choose

We offer two separate evening products. Their similar names do not make them interchangeable.

| Product | Dinner |
|---|---|
| [Samba and capoeira](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-samba-capoeira-night-show/) | Optional |
| [Show and churrascaria](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-night-show-churrascaria-dinner/) | Included in the excursion |

The first focuses on a musical and dance performance; the second combines a show with dinner at a churrascaria. Prices, menus, dance line-ups and guiding terms should not be carried over from one product to another. In particular, the published samba and capoeira show has no fixed ticket price or exact venue address.

## Choosing an evening for the show

Begin by considering how long you will stay in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) and what you have planned during the day. An extra late-night activity may be inconvenient after a flight and late check-in. If you depart early for the waterfalls or take another domestic flight the following day, agree on the return-to-hotel arrangements.

If your journey is mainly cultural, compare [Brazil cultural tours](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/). If exploring more of the country matters most, choose your main itinerary first and add a show where enough free time is available. In either case, confirm the venue and the content of the particular evening program instead of assuming a standard schedule.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with a samba show

### Is the samba and capoeira show included in the base price of every tour listed?

No. A link indicates that the excursion appears as a separate product within the tour; in several programs it is optional. Consult the list of included services for your selected trip.

### Can I book dinner together with the performance?

Yes. The standalone evening-show description lists dinner as an optional extra. Another product, “Rio by Night: Evening Show and Churrascaria Dinner,” includes dinner as part of that excursion.

### What is the difference between capoeira and samba?

Samba is a musical and dance tradition, while capoeira combines movement, play, combat elements and music. An evening show may feature stage interpretations of both.

### Does the show have a fixed duration and venue?

In Ada Tours' published description, the exact time and location depend on the chosen venue. Do not plan to return at a particular hour without a confirmed schedule.

## Evening show in Rio: samba, capoeira and Latin American dances

Music and dance play a prominent part in the cultural life of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/). Travelers often encounter them in the streets or during major festivals, but a separate evening performance offers a chance to see several stage traditions together.

We offer an **evening show featuring samba, capoeira and dances from Latin American countries**. The offer includes **admission to the performance at $120 per person**. Transportation is not included in this price, but it can be booked separately.

## Samba: music and stage dance

Samba is rooted in Afro-Brazilian musical traditions and Rio's urban culture. On stage, driving percussion, the dancers' skill and bright costumes draw audiences in. A short show, however, is not the same as a full Carnival parade with samba schools at the Sambadrome.

This distinction helps when planning a visit. Carnival follows seasonal dates and requires separate tickets, whereas an evening performance can be a standalone cultural activity during an ordinary city stay. **A Carnival parade and entry to the Sambadrome are not included** in this offer.

## Capoeira: movement, music and heritage

Capoeira brings together elements of martial art, dance, play and musical interaction. Traditionally, participants form a circle, or *roda*, accompanied by singing, clapping and rhythmic instruments.

UNESCO inscribed the **“Capoeira Circle”** on the Representative List of the Intangible Cultural Heritage of Humanity in 2014. This recognizes a cultural practice passed from masters to students; it does not mean every commercial stage show has its own UNESCO certification.

During a performance, it is fascinating to watch how artists communicate through movement and respond to the music. Audiences see the art but do not take a practical lesson: a capoeira class is not included in this excursion.

## Arranging a visit to the show

Confirm the current venue address, starting time, duration, seating arrangements and entry rules for the evening. The location and schedule must be clarified when booking; we do not guarantee one permanent venue or exact performance time.

**Transportation is charged separately.** If the show finishes late, arrange the journey there and back in advance, especially if you are staying in another part of Rio. An admission ticket on its own does not cover transport logistics.

Dinner, drinks and guest participation in the performance are not specified as part of the program. Any additional service needs to be explicitly confirmed, rather than assumed because this is an evening entertainment event.

## Choosing between the show and other cultural excursions

The show suits travelers who want to see several music and dance traditions in one evening. A separate city excursion is better for a deeper introduction to the history of Rio and its neighborhoods. The [Rio excursion catalog](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/) contains other options, while [Culture and History](/interests/culture-and-history/) brings together trips centered on local traditions.

Samba and capoeira are distinct arts, each with its own history, music and performance styles. Before choosing, find out which acts are included and how much time is allocated to each.

## Frequently asked questions about the evening show in Rio

### How much is admission?

Admission to the performance costs **$120 per person**.

### Is transportation included?

No. Transfers to and from the venue can be arranged at an additional cost.

### Is this Carnival at the Sambadrome?

No. It is a standalone evening stage performance featuring samba, capoeira and Latin American dances. A Carnival parade is a different event.

### Will there be a capoeira lesson?

No lesson is listed. The visit consists of watching a performance.

## Tours with an evening samba and capoeira show in Rio

An evening cultural experience in [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) can be a standalone addition to a longer journey. [“Rio Evening Show: Samba and Capoeira”](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-samba-capoeira-show-only/) combines dance numbers, capoeira elements and performances from Latin American traditions. Under the excursion's terms, the offer is **a show ticket without transportation**. The current listed price is **$120 per person**, and transport to and from the performance can be booked separately.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} with this specific standalone module. A confirmed itinerary is [“Dreams Come True: Champions' Parade, Iguazu and Buenos Aires”](/multi-country/tour/brazil-carnival-champions-parade-dreams/). It lasts 9 days and 8 nights, from February 12 to 20, 2027. The evening samba and capoeira show appears among **optional**, separately paid activities during free time in Rio.

## The show and the Champions' Parade: what's the difference?

It is easy to confuse 2 different cultural events during a festive Rio journey. **The Champions' Parade at the Sambadrome** is included in the named tour and scheduled for the evening of day two, with tickets and hotel–Sambadrome–hotel transfers. This is a Carnival parade featuring samba schools in a purpose-built venue.

**The evening samba and capoeira stage show** is a separate excursion product. The Ada Tours itinerary offers it after day three alongside other optional activities. Its ticket does not replace Sambadrome admission, automatically extend the parade or include transfers.

| Event | Confirmed inclusions |
|---|---|
| Champions' Parade | Tickets and transfers as part of the tour |
| Samba and capoeira show | $120 admission; transfers separately |

If Carnival is the main reason for your trip, begin with the dates and inclusions of the [Champions' Parade tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-carnival-champions-parade-dreams/). If you would also like another evening of staged performances, discuss the separate show. Both introduce dance culture, but their format and organization differ.

## How the show fits the rest of the itinerary

On the “Dreams Come True” journey, the first 3 nights are spent in Rio. Alongside Carnival, travelers visit Sugarloaf Mountain and Corcovado, then fly to Foz do Iguaçu to see the falls from both Brazilian and Argentine sides. The final stage is in Buenos Aires and includes city sightseeing and a tango show with dinner.

The sequence offers several different musical and cultural experiences: the Carnival parade in Rio, a possible extra samba and capoeira show, and an included tango show later in Argentina. But **the optional Rio performance is not part of the paid base package**. Budget separately for its ticket and transport, and allow enough rest before the next sightseeing day or flight.

Other optional activities listed for day three include a Guanabara Bay boat trip, historic Rio, a helicopter excursion, the botanical garden and active outings. These products have different terms and prices; you do not need to book everything just to complete the list. Your choice depends on free time and compatible schedules.

## What to confirm before attending

For the stage show, agree on the start time, meeting point and return transfer in advance. The standalone [“Samba and Capoeira Show” excursion](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-samba-capoeira-show-only/) specifies admission but does not state a fixed performance duration or venue address. Do not assign arbitrary end times or promise that a driver will already be waiting outside.

As part of the Carnival itinerary, we help coordinate an optional evening with the main excursions and transfers. If you visit Rio outside the Carnival tour dates, confirm availability of the specific show separately: an excursion page does not by itself mean there are daily performances.

To compare other cultural journeys, browse [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) and [Brazil culture and history itineraries](/interests/culture-and-history/tours/brazil/), checking whether the particular performance is included.

## Frequently asked questions about tours featuring the samba and capoeira show

### Is the show included in the Champions' Parade tour price?

No. The [Carnival tour](/multi-country/tour/brazil-carnival-champions-parade-dreams/) includes the Champions' Parade, while the evening samba and capoeira show is an additional, separately paid excursion.

### How much is the evening-show ticket?

The current standalone-excursion description specifies **$120 per person**. This covers the show only, without transportation.

### Can I use my Sambadrome ticket for this show?

No. The Champions' Parade and the stage show are separate events with separate tickets.

### Are there other evening shows on the tour?

Yes. The [“Dreams Come True” itinerary](/multi-country/tour/brazil-carnival-champions-parade-dreams/) includes a tango show with dinner in Buenos Aires. It takes place during the Argentine stage and does not replace an evening show in Rio.

### Can I arrange transportation to the show?

The excursion description allows transfers to be booked separately. Agree on the price and terms before attending.

## Cycling through Rio's South Zone: beaches, cliffs and a lagoon

The South Zone of [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) is well suited to exploring by bicycle. In a relatively compact area, an open Atlantic coastline sits beside residential neighborhoods, rocky headlands and a freshwater lagoon. Our route visits **Copacabana, Ipanema, Arpoador, Leblon and Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon**. Stops along the beaches offer a view of the city that feels very different from seeing it from a car.

The excursion is for travelers interested in the urban environment itself: people along the waterfront, ocean views, changing beach neighborhoods and mountains rising behind the buildings. It is described as a relaxed coastal ride, not a competitive race, challenging mountain-bike route or trip into a national park.

## What you will see along the route

**Copacabana** is known for its broad sandy beach and promenade with a distinctive wave-patterned pavement. It reveals the resort side of a major city: beach life, hotels and a busy everyday scene.

**Ipanema** offers open views of the ocean and mountains to the west of the beach. **Arpoador** occupies a rocky section between Ipanema and Copacabana. From a stop here, you can see the coastline change direction and buildings meet the rocks.

**Leblon** continues the coastal stretch west of Ipanema, where the mountains seem especially close to the sea. **Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon** offers a contrasting view, with calm water, paths and surrounding hills instead of surf. The transition from beaches to lagoon makes the ride varied.

The places listed are confirmed by the itinerary. Their exact order, stopping points and length of breaks are arranged for each departure; the list should not be treated as a minute-by-minute schedule.

## How demanding is the bike ride?

The defining feature of a Zona Sul cycling tour is the urban traffic environment. Riders may share nearby space with pedestrians, runners, other cyclists and stretches of road used by cars. Even on a gentle route, you should be able to start, brake and keep a safe distance confidently. Experience of long-distance sports cycling is unnecessary, but basic bicycle-riding skills are essential.

Southern Rio has cycling infrastructure along the coast. The city also sometimes creates temporary cycling areas on Sundays and public holidays. Check the specific arrangements and access for the date of your ride: temporary traffic management is not the same as a permanent cycle lane.

Before departure, agree on bicycle size and type, helmet availability, guiding format, starting point and return arrangements. Bicycle hire, helmets, a private instructor and transfers **are not confirmed** as included services.

## When to ride and what to bring

Heat, humidity and strong sunlight matter on this excursion. Morning hours are often more comfortable than midday; in hot weather, avoid lengthy stops in exposed areas. Rain can reduce grip on paving and asphalt, while strong coastal winds may make riding more difficult.

Bring water, sunscreen, lightweight clothing suitable for pedaling and shoes with stable soles. A small backpack is preferable to a bag you need to carry in your hand. Protect your phone from rain. Discuss possible changes of time or itinerary in advance in case of poor weather.

Rio is suitable for cycling at different times of year, but comfort depends on the weather that day. Actual heat and rainfall matter more than any universal promise of a “best season.”

## Bicycle tour or classic Rio sightseeing?

Cycling offers **a continuous introduction to beachfront neighborhoods**, rather than an attempt to see every famous city landmark on one trip. Corcovado, Sugarloaf Mountain and the historic center are better left to a separate sightseeing day. Explore alternatives in the [Rio excursion catalog](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/).

For natural panoramas involving a hike, compare this with [Pedra Bonita trekking](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/pedra-bonita-hike/). That trip aims to reach a summit viewpoint; this one focuses on the oceanfront, city streets and lagoon. On a longer vacation, combine cycling with [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/), leaving time for beaches and other neighborhoods.

This route is especially useful on a first trip to Rio for understanding how its famous beaches connect. It also suits returning visitors who have seen the major viewpoints and want to spend part of the day being active.

## Frequently asked questions about the Zona Sul bike tour

### Which neighborhoods are included?

Copacabana, Ipanema, Arpoador, Leblon and Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon. Our cycle route visits these locations.

### How many kilometers and hours does it take?

The exact distance and duration are agreed before departure. Confirm the distance, start and finish points, stops and expected pace.

### Are bicycles and helmets provided?

Hire and equipment must be arranged before the trip. These conditions need confirmation during booking.

### Is Corcovado included?

There is no confirmation that Corcovado is part of the Zona Sul cycling program. The ascent to Corcovado and a visit to Sugarloaf Mountain are better treated as separate Rio excursions.

## Tours featuring a bike ride through southern Rio de Janeiro

If you would like to discover [Rio de Janeiro](/brazil/place/rio-de-janeiro/) without a long car-based excursion immediately after landing, a bicycle ride through the city's southern coastal neighborhoods, Zona Sul, is an option. The [“South Zone Rio Bike Tour”](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-south-zone-bike-tour/) covers Copacabana, Ipanema, Arpoador, Leblon and Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon. The main sights are the Atlantic Ocean, urban waterfront and lagoon surrounded by residential areas.

Our selection includes {{catalog.toursCountPhrase}} using this standalone excursion module. One of our itineraries is [“Rio de Janeiro – Amazon – Iguazu Falls”](/brazil/tour/rio-de-janeiro-amazon-iguazu-falls/). The bike outing appears **after day one** as an optional activity during free time following arrival in Rio. It does not make the whole multi-region journey a cycling tour.

## Why the ride comes at the start of the trip

Day one of the “Rio – Amazon – Iguazu” itinerary is devoted to arrival, airport reception and transfer to the hotel. The remaining time is free, so visitors may choose to explore Rio's beach districts. Copacabana, Ipanema, Arpoador and Leblon lie along the ocean, while the lagoon provides a different view away from the sandy shoreline.

The [bike tour](/brazil/rio-de-janeiro/rio-south-zone-bike-tour/) links these places into one city outing. However, its confirmed description **does not specify an exact duration, price, included bicycle hire or starting location**. All these details need to be arranged, especially when your flight lands on the same day. Do not infer a particular level of physical exertion or included equipment from the words “bike tour.”

After the coastal introduction, the main journey continues in a different style: Rio's Sugarloaf Mountain, historic center and Corcovado, followed by the Amazon with river and forest excursions. Towards the end, travelers see [Iguazu Falls](/brazil/place/foz-do-iguacu/) on the Brazilian and Argentine sides according to the itinerary. Cycling is an introduction to a geographically diverse journey, not its central activity on every day.

## Who will enjoy adding the bike tour?

This option suits travelers who like being outdoors and exploring a city in motion. Compared with a car-based sightseeing excursion, cycling allows more frequent stops near beaches but requires readiness for the weather, sun and urban traffic. Bring water, sun protection and comfortable clothes. Discuss the precise route, guiding, equipment and road safety with the organizer.

Consider 3 things before booking. First, your arrival time: after a long international flight, allow time for formalities and the hotel transfer. Second, your usual activity level: a bike ride may not suit all group members equally. Third, the next day's schedule: significant Rio attractions are already planned, so it helps to preserve your energy.

For a more leisurely introduction, you can walk independently along the promenade and see the main architectural and natural sights on subsequent included excursions. If active routes are your primary interest, compare [adventure tours in Brazil](/interests/adventure/tours/brazil/) and check which activities are mandatory.

## Choosing a tour that offers this excursion

Start with the complete route. [“Rio de Janeiro – Amazon – Iguazu”](/brazil/tour/rio-de-janeiro-amazon-iguazu-falls/) is designed to introduce several regions on one trip: an oceanfront metropolis, rainforest and a huge waterfall system. The bike ride is offered in free time on day one; its public description does not state the activity's duration or price.

Other [Brazil tours](/brazil/tour/) may include Copacabana walks, Rio sightseeing or separate sports activities, but similar geography does not mean they contain this exact canonical Zona Sul bike excursion. Compare the day-by-day itinerary and the list of included and optional activities. We can help coordinate the sequence so an optional ride does not interfere with transfers or mandatory sightseeing.

## Frequently asked questions about tours with a Zona Sul bike ride

### Where does the route go?

The description specifies Copacabana, Ipanema, Arpoador, Leblon and Rodrigo de Freitas Lagoon. These are southern Rio locations featuring beaches, a waterfront and residential areas.

### Is cycling included in the main trip price?

On the [“Rio – Amazon – Iguazu” tour](/brazil/tour/rio-de-janeiro-amazon-iguazu-falls/), it appears among activities available on the first free day. Its inclusion in the base package is unconfirmed, so terms must be agreed separately.

### Can I cycle straight after arrival?

Possibly, if your arrival time and energy allow. Check your flight landing time, hotel transfer and available excursion slot in advance; the current description does not specify a fixed start time.

### Are a bicycle and safety helmet supplied?

The published description does not list equipment. Confirm bicycle hire, a helmet and guiding before reserving the outing.
